title: Christ Our Shepherd
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ our Shepherd means that Jesus lovingly leads, feeds, guards, corrects, restores, and keeps His sheep. He is the good Shepherd who lays down His life for His people.
summary: Christ our Shepherd means that Jesus lovingly leads, feeds, guards, corrects, restores, and keeps His sheep. He is the good Shepherd who lays down His life for His people.
christFocus: Jesus reveals Himself as the Good Shepherd who knows His sheep, gives His life for them, gathers them, protects them, and brings them safely to the Father.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture often describes God’s care for His people in shepherd language. Jesus takes this identity to Himself, declaring that He is the good Shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep.

Christ knows His sheep personally. They are not a nameless crowd to Him. He calls, leads, feeds, protects, and gathers them by His voice.

His shepherd care includes rescue and correction. Wandering sheep need restoration, wounded sheep need care, and threatened sheep need protection from thieves and wolves.

The Shepherd who died is also the great Shepherd raised from the dead. He equips His people, keeps them, and will appear as the Chief Shepherd with unfading reward.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel lost, unwanted, weak, or unsafe. Christ our Shepherd gives comfort that believers are not abandoned to care for themselves.

This doctrine also shapes pastoral ministry. Under-shepherds must care for Christ’s sheep with His heart, not use them for pride, power, or personal gain.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Listen to the voice of Christ your Shepherd. Follow Him when He leads, return when you wander, receive His correction, and trust His care in valleys as well as green pastures. Care for others with the gentleness and truth of the Shepherd who cares for you.
